text: If one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Walk boldly toward your dreams and live the life you imagine. Success will come in ways you did not expect.

text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Live with attention to what truly matters, so you never look back and feel you missed your own life.

text: However mean your life is, meet it and live it; do not shun it and call it hard names.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Even if your life feels small or hard, face it honestly. Do not run from it or insult it.

text: Love your life, poor as it is.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Value the life you have, even when you do not have much.

text: If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer. Let him step to the music which he hears, however measured or far away.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: If you are not like the people around you, that is fine. Follow your own path at your own pace.

text: Only that day dawns to which we are awake. There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: A new day only begins for us when we are truly awake to it. Far more is still possible.

text: A man is rich in proportion to the number of things which he can afford to let alone.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: True wealth is not owning more. It is being happy without needing so many things.

text: Things do not change; we change.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: The world often stays the same. What changes is us and how we see it.

text: Every morning was a cheerful invitation to make my life of equal simplicity, and I may say innocence, with Nature herself.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Each morning invited him to live simply and purely, in step with nature.

text: It is never too late to give up our prejudices.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: You can drop an unfair opinion at any age. It is always possible to think better.

text: What a man thinks of himself, that it is which determines, or rather indicates, his fate.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: What you believe about yourself shapes the life you end up living.

text: I know of no more encouraging fact than the unquestionable ability of man to elevate his life by a conscious endeavor.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: The most hopeful truth is that anyone can improve their life through steady, conscious effort.

text: If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Big dreams are not wasted. Keep them high, then do the real work that makes them solid.

text: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Morning is not a time on the clock. It is the feeling of being fresh and alive inside.

text: To affect the quality of the day, that is the highest of arts.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: The greatest skill is making today better through how you live it.

text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Believe in yourself. Everyone has something inside that responds to this truth.

text: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Real peace does not come from people or things. It comes from within you.

text: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Great things need excitement and energy. Without passion, nothing big gets done.

text: The only reward of virtue, is virtue; the only way to have a friend is to be one.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Doing good is its own reward. If you want a friend, be a good friend first.

text: A friend may well be reckoned the masterpiece of nature.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: A true friend is one of the finest things life can give you.

text: Insist on yourself; never imitate.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Be fully yourself and trust your own gifts. Do not copy other people.

text: A man is relieved and gay when he has put his heart into his work and done his best.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: You feel light and happy after giving your whole heart to your work and doing your best.

text: Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: To be your true self, you must sometimes refuse to follow the crowd.

text: Always do what you are afraid to do.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Grow by facing the things that scare you. Courage comes from doing them.

text: Self-trust is the essence of heroism.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Being a hero begins with trusting yourself.

text: Though we travel the world over to find the beautiful, we must carry it with us, or we find it not.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: You can travel everywhere, but you only see beauty if you already carry it inside you.

text: Light, my light, the world-filling light, the eye-kissing light, heart-sweetening light!
author: Rabindranath Tagore
meaning: A joyful song of thanks for light, which fills the world and warms the heart.

text: Men are anxious to improve their circumstances, but are unwilling to improve themselves.
author: James Allen
meaning: People want a better life, but they do not want to change themselves. Real change starts within.

text: Dream lofty dreams, and as you dream, so shall you become.
author: James Allen
meaning: Aim high in your dreams, because you slowly grow into what you dream of.

text: Your Vision is the promise of what you shall one day be; your Ideal is the prophecy of what you shall at last unveil.
author: James Allen
meaning: Your dreams and ideals show the person you can become one day.

text: Calmness of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom.
author: James Allen
meaning: A calm mind is one of the finest signs of true wisdom.

text: Self-control is strength; Right Thought is mastery; Calmness is power.
author: James Allen
meaning: Controlling yourself gives strength, good thinking gives skill, and staying calm gives power.

text: The dreamers are the saviours of the world.
author: James Allen
meaning: People who imagine a better world are the ones who help create it.

text: Cherish your visions; cherish your ideals.
author: James Allen
meaning: Hold your dreams and values close, and protect them.

text: Thought allied fearlessly to purpose becomes creative force.
author: James Allen
meaning: When your thinking is joined to a clear goal, without fear, it can create real results.

text: He who has conquered doubt and fear has conquered failure.
author: James Allen
meaning: Beat your doubt and fear, and failure can no longer stop you.

text: Circumstance does not make the man; it reveals him to himself.
author: James Allen
meaning: Your situation does not make you who you are. It shows you who you already are.

text: I exist as I am, that is enough.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: You do not have to prove anything. Being yourself is enough.

text: Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road, Healthy, free, the world before me.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Set out with a happy heart. You are well, you are free, and the whole world is open to you.

text: I am large, I contain multitudes.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: A person is full of many sides, and they do not all have to match.

text: That you are here—that life exists and identity, That the powerful play goes on, and you may contribute a verse.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: You are alive, and life goes on like a great play. You can add your own line to it.

text: To me every hour of the light and dark is a miracle, Every cubic inch of space is a miracle.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Every moment and every small part of the world is a wonder, if you really notice it.

text: Henceforth I ask not good-fortune, I myself am good-fortune.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: From now on I will not wait for luck. I make my own good fortune.

text: I am larger, better than I thought, I did not know I held so much goodness.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: I am bigger and kinder than I knew. There was more good in me than I imagined.

text: This above all: to thine own self be true.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Most of all, be honest with yourself and stay true to who you are.

text: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Events are not good or bad on their own. Your thoughts about them decide how they feel.

text: We know what we are, but know not what we may be.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: We know who we are today, but we have no idea how much we can become.

text: The readiness is all.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: You cannot control what comes. What matters is being prepared for it.

text: Give every man thy ear, but few thy voice.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Listen to everyone, but speak to only a few. Hear more than you say.

text: How far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: A small candle shines far, and one good deed brightens a dark world in the same way.

text: Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: True love does not depend on looks. It sees the person inside.

text: Though she be but little, she is fierce.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Do not judge by size. A small person can be very strong and brave.

text: My bounty is as boundless as the sea, My love as deep; the more I give to thee, The more I have, for both are infinite.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Love is like the endless sea. The more I give, the more I have.

text: There is a tide in the affairs of men, Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Life brings moments of opportunity. Act when the time is right and it can carry you to success.

text: Men at some time are masters of their fates.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: At certain moments, people have the power to shape their own future.

text: Screw your courage to the sticking-place, And we'll not fail.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Gather all your courage and hold on firmly. If you do, you will not fail.

text: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Life's troubles do not scare me, because I am learning how to handle them.

text: Love is a great beautifier.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Love makes people look and feel more beautiful.

text: Never get tired of trying, and never think it is impossible to conquer your fault.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Keep trying and never believe that your faults are too strong to overcome.

text: There is always light behind the clouds.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Even in hard times, hope is still there. Bad days always hide something brighter.

text: Have regular hours for work and play, make each day both useful and pleasant.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Keep a balance of work and fun, so each day is both useful and enjoyable.

text: Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Every day is a fresh start. Yesterday's mistakes do not have to follow you.

text: I'm so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Enjoy the small seasons and beauties of life, and feel glad that they exist.

text: It's delightful when your imaginations come true, isn't it?
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: It is a special joy when the things you once imagined really happen.

text: Kindred spirits are not so scarce as I used to think.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: People who truly understand you are easier to find than you once thought.

text: "Dear old world," she murmured, "you are very lovely, and I am glad to be alive in you."
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Pause to love the world and feel thankful just to be alive in it.

text: All things great are wound up with all things little.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Great things are always connected to small things, so small things matter too.

text: Next to trying and winning, the best thing is trying and failing.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Trying and failing is still valuable. It is far better than never trying at all.

text: It's good to be alive and to be going home.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Simple things, like being alive and going home, are real happiness.

text: Looking forward to things is half the pleasure of them.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Being excited about something good is already half the joy of it.

text: Where you tend a rose, my lad, A thistle cannot grow.
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
meaning: Care for good things in your mind and life, and there will be no room for bad things to grow.

text: At first people refuse to believe that a strange new thing can be done, then they begin to hope it can be done, then they see it can be done.
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
meaning: New ideas seem impossible at first. Then people hope, then they see it, and soon it feels normal.

text: Thoughts—just mere thoughts—are as powerful as electric batteries—as good for one as sunlight is.
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
meaning: Your thoughts have real power. Good thoughts can heal and strengthen you, like sunlight.

text: Think only of the past as its remembrance gives you pleasure.
author: Jane Austen
meaning: Do not carry past pain. Remember only the parts that make you happy.

text: My courage always rises at every attempt to intimidate me.
author: Jane Austen
meaning: When someone tries to frighten me, I only become braver.

text: There is nothing like staying at home for real comfort.
author: Jane Austen
meaning: Home gives a comfort that nothing else in the world can.

text: Know your own happiness.
author: Jane Austen
meaning: Notice how much you already have, and be thankful for your own happiness.

text: Heaven knows we need never be ashamed of our tears, for they are rain upon the blinding dust of earth, overlying our hard hearts.
author: Charles Dickens
meaning: Crying is nothing to be ashamed of. Tears wash the heart clean, as rain washes dust away.

text: Whatever I have tried to do in life, I have tried with all my heart to do well.
author: Charles Dickens
meaning: Whatever work I took up, I gave it my whole heart. That is the secret of doing things well.

text: Never do tomorrow what you can do today. Procrastination is the thief of time.
author: Charles Dickens
meaning: Do it today. Putting things off quietly steals your time.

text: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
author: George Eliot
meaning: We are here to make life a little easier for each other.

text: The growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts.
author: George Eliot
meaning: The world gets better through small, quiet good deeds that nobody ever writes about.

text: Everything comes in time to him who knows how to wait.
author: Leo Tolstoy
meaning: With patience, the right things come at the right time.

text: I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I'll go to it laughing.
author: Herman Melville
meaning: I do not know what the future will bring, but I will meet it with a smile.

text: It's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
author: Lewis Carroll
meaning: Do not live in the past. You have changed, and you are not the same person now.

text: Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it.
author: Lewis Carroll
meaning: Every experience can teach you something, if you look for the lesson.

text: Who in the world am I? Ah, that's the great puzzle!
author: Lewis Carroll
meaning: Knowing who you really are is one of life's biggest and most interesting questions.

text: The mind is its own place, and in itself Can make a Heaven of Hell, a Hell of Heaven.
author: John Milton
meaning: Your mind decides how you experience life. It can make a bad place good, or a good place bad.

text: Simplify, simplify.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Make life simpler. Let go of what you do not need.

text: I had three chairs in my house; one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Keep room in life for quiet time alone, for close friends, and for the wider world.

text: I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Time alone can be good company. You do not always need other people.

text: Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Truth matters more than love, money, or fame.

text: Say what you have to say, not what you ought.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Speak honestly. Say what you really think, not what others expect from you.

text: We must learn to reawaken and keep ourselves awake, not by mechanical aids, but by an infinite expectation of the dawn.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Stay awake to life through hope for each new day, not through outside pushes.

text: Every child begins the world again, to some extent.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Every child starts life fresh, with a chance to see the world in a new way.

text: I love a broad margin to my life.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Leave open space in your life. Do not fill every hour with work.

text: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Time flows past like a river. Use it calmly and enjoy it, without being afraid of it.

text: Books are the treasured wealth of the world and the fit inheritance of generations and nations.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Books are humanity's great treasure, passed from one generation to the next.

text: How many a man has dated a new era in his life from the reading of a book!
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: One book can change a person's life and begin a new chapter for them.

text: Goodness is the only investment that never fails.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Being good always pays back. It never loses its value.

text: Not till we are lost, in other words not till we have lost the world, do we begin to find ourselves.
author: Henry David Thoreau
meaning: Sometimes we must lose our way before we truly discover who we are.

text: To believe your own thought, to believe that what is true for you in your private heart is true for all men,—that is genius.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Trust your own deep thoughts. What feels true in your heart is often true for others too.

text: What I must do is all that concerns me, not what the people think.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Do your own duty. Do not worry about what people will say.

text: The voyage of the best ship is a zigzag line of a hundred tacks.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Even the best journey is full of turns. A crooked path can still reach the goal.

text: The power which resides in him is new in nature, and none but he knows what that is which he can do, nor does he know until he has tried.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Everyone has a unique power, and you only learn what you can do by trying.

text: Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Stay honest with yourself. That matters more than anything else.

text: These roses under my window make no reference to former roses or to better ones; they are for what they are.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
meaning: Roses do not compare themselves with others. They simply are. Be happy being yourself.

text: Isn't it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about?
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: The world is full of things to learn. How exciting that is!

text: Now there is a bend in it. I don't know what lies around the bend, but I'm going to believe that the best does.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: My plans have changed and I cannot see what comes next, but I choose to believe it will be good.

text: I don't want to be anyone but myself, even if I go uncomforted by diamonds all my life.
author: L. M. Montgomery
meaning: Be happy being yourself, even if you never become rich.

text: Be worthy, love, and love will come.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Become a good person and love will find you.

text: Don't let the sun go down upon your anger.
author: Louisa May Alcott
meaning: Do not stay angry until nightfall. Forgive and make peace before the day ends.

text: I shall live forever—and ever—and ever!
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
meaning: A child's joyful feeling that he is healthy, alive, and full of life.

text: Trifles make the sum of life.
author: Charles Dickens
meaning: Small things, added together, make up your whole life.

text: One must be poor to know the luxury of giving!
author: George Eliot
meaning: Someone who has known hardship feels the real joy of giving to others.

text: It is a narrow mind which cannot look at a subject from various points of view.
author: George Eliot
meaning: A wise person looks at things from many sides, not just their own.

text: People are almost always better than their neighbors think they are.
author: George Eliot
meaning: Most people are kinder and better than others give them credit for.

text: Love hinders death. Love is life.
author: Leo Tolstoy
meaning: Love is stronger than death. To love is to truly live.

text: All, everything that I understand, I understand only because I love.
author: Leo Tolstoy
meaning: Love is what helps us understand people and the world.

text: Pure and complete sorrow is as impossible as pure and complete joy.
author: Leo Tolstoy
meaning: No feeling lasts completely. Even in sorrow, there is some light, and even in joy, some shadow.

text: There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others.
author: Jane Austen
meaning: I will not let others scare me into giving up what I want.

text: The Vision that you glorify in your mind, the Ideal that you enthrone in your heart—this you will build your life by, this you will become.
author: James Allen
meaning: What you hold in your mind and heart guides your life, and you grow into it.

text: Let a man radically alter his thoughts, and he will be astonished at the rapid transformation it will effect in the material conditions of his life.
author: James Allen
meaning: Change your thoughts deeply, and your outer life will change faster than you expect.

text: A man cannot directly choose his circumstances, but he can choose his thoughts, and so indirectly, yet surely, shape his circumstances.
author: James Allen
meaning: You cannot always choose what happens, but you can choose your thoughts, and they shape your life.

text: Keep your hand firmly upon the helm of thought.
author: James Allen
meaning: Stay in charge of your thoughts, just as a captain steers a ship.

text: As he thinks, so he is; as he continues to think, so he remains.
author: James Allen
meaning: Your thoughts shape you. Keep the same thoughts, and you will stay the same.

text: The greatest achievement was at first and for a time a dream.
author: James Allen
meaning: Every great success began as just a dream.

text: Dreams are the seedlings of realities.
author: James Allen
meaning: Today's dreams are the seeds of tomorrow's real things.

text: He who would accomplish little must sacrifice little; he who would achieve much must sacrifice much.
author: James Allen
meaning: Bigger goals need bigger effort and sacrifice. What you give decides what you get.

text: The more tranquil a man becomes, the greater is his success, his influence, his power for good.
author: James Allen
meaning: The calmer you are, the more you succeed and the more good you can do.

text: Thou hast made me known to friends whom I knew not.
author: Rabindranath Tagore
meaning: Thanks for bringing good people into my life, people I did not know before.

text: Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high; Where knowledge is free.
author: Rabindranath Tagore
meaning: A prayer for a place where people live without fear, with pride, and where learning is open to all.

text: He is there where the tiller is tilling the hard ground and where the pathmaker is breaking stones.
author: Rabindranath Tagore
meaning: God is found among hard-working people, not only in temples.

text: Failing to fetch me at first keep encouraged, Missing me one place search another, I stop somewhere waiting for you.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: If you do not find what you are looking for at first, keep going. It is waiting for you.

text: Be not discouraged, keep on, there are divine things well envelop'd.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Do not lose heart. Keep going, because wonderful things are still ahead.

text: I swear to you there are divine things more beautiful than words can tell.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Some things are so beautiful that words can never fully describe them.

text: Why, who makes much of a miracle? As to me I know of nothing else but miracles.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Why call only rare events miracles? Everything in life is a miracle.

text: Not I, not any one else can travel that road for you, You must travel it for yourself.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Others can guide you, but only you can walk your own path.

text: All goes onward and outward, nothing collapses.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Life keeps moving forward. Nothing is really lost or wasted.

text: Allons! the road is before us!
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Come on, let's go! A whole journey is waiting for us.

text: Now voyager sail thou forth to seek and find.
author: Walt Whitman
meaning: Go forward bravely, and search for new things to discover.

text: Let your own discretion be your tutor.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Use your own good judgment as your teacher.

text: How poor are they that have not patience! What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Be patient. Every wound heals slowly, little by little.

text: Our bodies are our gardens, to the which our wills are gardeners.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: You shape your body and your life by what you choose, as a gardener shapes a garden.

text: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Go wisely and slowly. People who rush are the ones who trip and fall.

text: Come what come may, Time and the hour runs through the roughest day.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Whatever happens, time moves on, and even the hardest day will end.

text: Things without all remedy Should be without regard: what's done is done.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Do not worry about what cannot be changed. What's done is done, so move on.

text: The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, But in ourselves.
author: William Shakespeare
meaning: Do not blame luck or fate. Our lives depend on our own choices.

text: "Begin at the beginning," the King said gravely, "and go on till you come to the end: then stop."
author: Lewis Carroll
meaning: Start at the start, keep going to the end, and then stop. Simple steps get things done.

text: What though the field be lost? All is not lost.
author: John Milton
meaning: Losing one battle is not losing everything. There is always something left to fight for.

text: Accuse not Nature, she hath done her part; Do thou but thine.
author: John Milton
meaning: Do not blame what you were given. Life did its part, so now do yours.

text: Solitude sometimes is best society, And short retirement urges sweet return.
author: John Milton
meaning: Being alone for a while can be good for you, and it makes coming back to others sweeter.

text: Such as thy thoughts and ordinary cogitations are, such will thy mind be in time.
author: Marcus Aurelius
meaning: You become what you think about every day. Choose your thoughts with care.

text: Look within; within is the fountain of all good. Such a fountain, where springing waters can never fail, so thou dig still deeper and deeper.
author: Marcus Aurelius
meaning: All good is inside you. Keep looking deeper, and you will always find more strength.

text: Meddle not with many things, if thou wilt live cheerfully.
author: Marcus Aurelius
meaning: Do not take on too many things. A simpler life is a happier life.
